cases.name: success
steps: The continuation opens the normal starter picker; Apply creates only an ordinary draft and Save adds exactly the unchanged official signal TXT plus its registration.

Explicit Return refreshes the catalog after Save while retaining the same staged identities and second instance; no source is automatically selected. Explicit source selection, Review and Save create the first behavior, and ordinary event mapping Save persists only its reviewed manifest.
The sole real Godot plan, build and headless run emit context_ready from the second actual scene instance with that exact stable binding and unchanged official signal arguments.

cases.name: cancel
steps: Cancelling the starter picker creates no document; explicit Return restores the same Bevy profile, path, object and binding identities and second instance.
Creating then cancelling the ordinary Rust TXT draft also writes nothing and preserves the original configuration through explicit Return.
Explicitly discarding the final staged continuation clears the return action and leaves all two-document author bytes unchanged.

steps: The continuation opens the normal starter picker; Apply creates only an ordinary draft and Save adds exactly the unchanged official signal TXT plus its registration.

limitations: Each case initializes the official blank template layout with zero authored documents, registered documents or assets; desktop-library folder selection, installed Tauri and Android are outside this browser case.

Definitions, two-instance scenes, official ordinary TXT drafts and behavior manifests are created with real Studio controls. The signal starter and generated Godot source are never edited by the driver.
The changed-source case uses the real ordinary document HTTP API and optimistic version check to simulate another editor, then restores the exact original scene bytes through that same API.
Only the successful case performs one Godot plan, one build and one headless run. This verifies a first-behavior continuation, not a complete game or native input workflow.
